attachments.origin_landmark: scaphoid fossa and the medial pterygoid plate, and the cartilage of the pharyngotympanic tube
attachments.insertion_landmark: palatine aponeurosis, after hooking around the pterygoid hamulus

actions: opens the pharyngotympanic tube during swallowing and yawning

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: The ONE palatal muscle not supplied by the vagus -- it takes CN V3, because it develops from the first pharyngeal arch. Its tendon turns a right angle around the pterygoid hamulus, which acts as a pulley. Failure of its tubal action underlies the middle ear effusions of cleft palate.

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Not an ultrasound-guided technique -- injected transorally (or, in some reports, trans-palatally/intrapalatally) under direct visualization. The most specific published landmark: inject at the level of the pterygoid hamulus, into the lateral soft palate, which is where the tensor veli palatini tendon turns around the hamulus before fanning into the palatine aponeurosis. Also described as a percutaneous/EMG-guided injection of the paratubal muscle group (tensor veli palatini, levator veli palatini, salpingopharyngeus together) for patulous eustachian tube.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: For palatal myoclonus presenting with clicking tinnitus, tensor veli palatini is the first-choice initial injection site (as opposed to musculus uvulae, used when perceived palatal movement rather than tinnitus predominates). For patulous eustachian tube/autophonia, diagnosis and post-treatment response are confirmed with posterior rhinoscopy (nasopharyngoscopy) and impedance/tympanometric audiometry showing normalized tympanic ventilation.
structures_at_risk: ascending palatine and lesser palatine vessels running with the muscle near the hamulus

tensor tympani indirectly, via the shared trigeminal (CN V3) innervation and the tensor veli palatini's mechanical link to eustachian tube/tympanic membrane tension -- the rationale for using palatal/tensor veli palatini injection to treat some forms of objective/palatal tinnitus and middle ear myoclonus
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Three overlapping but distinct indications in the literature: (1) palatal myoclonus with clicking tinnitus -- transoral injection at the pterygoid hamulus/lateral soft palate, 2.5 U initial dose, titrated on follow-up; (2) patulous eustachian tube / autophonia -- EMG-guided injection of tensor veli palatini (with levator veli palatini and salpingopharyngeus) based on the hypothesis that abnormal paratubal muscle activity keeps the tube patulous; symptom relief reported for about 9 months in one case; (3) middle ear myoclonus / objective tinnitus and forced-eyelid-closure-syndrome tinnitus -- trans-palatal BoNT into the tensor veli palatini aponeurosis, used as a less invasive alternative or adjunct to surgical tensor tympani/stapedius tendon division. All are niche, case-report/small-series-level evidence rather than large trials.
